facts.statement: Richard Lydekker first described Barilium as a species of Iguanodon in 1888.
facts.quote: Barilium is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur which was first described as a species of Iguanodon (I. dawsoni) by Richard Lydekker in 1888

facts.statement: The specific name dawsoni honors Charles Dawson, who collected the holotype in the 1880s.
facts.quote: the specific epithet honouring the discoverer Charles Dawson, who collected the holotype during the 1880s

facts.statement: David Norman reclassified Barilium as a separate genus in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010 it was reclassified as a separate genus by David Norman

facts.statement: Two partial skeletons of Barilium were found near St Leonards-on-Sea in East Sussex, England.
facts.quote: It is known from two partial skeletons found near St Leonards-on-Sea in East Sussex, England

facts.statement: Fossils of Barilium come from the middle Valanginian-age Lower Cretaceous Wadhurst Clay.
facts.quote: from the middle Valanginian-age Lower Cretaceous Wadhurst Clay

facts.statement: Barilium was a robust iguanodontian estimated to be 8 meters long.
facts.quote: Barilium was a robust iguanodontian estimated at 8 m long

facts.statement: Barilium had large vertebrae with short neural spines, resembling those of Camptosaurus.
facts.quote: Barilium was more robust than Hypselospinus, with large Camptosaurus-like vertebrae featuring short neural spines

facts.statement: Kenneth Carpenter and Yusuke Ishida independently assigned Barilium to the genus Torilion in 2010, making Torilion a junior synonym.
facts.quote: Later in 2010, Kenneth Carpenter and Yusuke Ishida independently assigned it to the new genus Torilion, which is thus a junior objective synonym of Barilium

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Barilium outside the Hadrosauriformes clade, grouping it with Hypselospinus and Ouranosaurus.
facts.quote: Barilium was placed outside the styracosternan clade Hadrosauriformes, in a clade also containing Hypselospinus and Ouranosaurus

facts.statement: Barilium lived approximately 138 million years ago during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 138 millones de años durante el Valanginiense en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: The genus name Barilium is derived from the Greek word for "heavy" and the Latin word for "ilium".
facts.quote: El nombre del género Barilium se deriva del griego barys, "pesado", y del latín ilium, "hueso ilíaco"

facts.statement: Barilium belongs to the unranked family Iguanodontia.
The time range for Barilium is from the Valanginian to the Barremian, between 137.05 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Barremian (137.05 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Barilium is the family Iguanodontidae.

rejected.statement: A 2026 study by Sacamoto and colleagues treated Barilium and Kukufeldia as distinct taxa.
rejected.quote: In their 2026 description of Paludohadros, Sacamoto and colleagues treated Barilium and Kukufeldia as distinct taxa
